resources.string: Bluetooth name and PIN of the controller\'s module, and VESC Remote pairing
A module on the UART port gets no answers

The input app is set to one without UART, so the firmware doesn\'t run the UART port. A Bluetooth or WiFi module plugged into it can\'t reach the controller. Choose an app with UART in App settings, General, or use the board\'s built-in radio.

The input app is set to ADC, which uses the UART pins as buttons. A Bluetooth or WiFi module plugged into the UART port can\'t reach the controller. Choose ADC and UART in App settings, General, if a module is connected there.
Sets the name phones see when they scan, and the PIN they need to connect. Leave a field empty to go back to the module\'s default name or to turn the PIN off.
This controller\'s Bluetooth module can\'t be set up from here
Its firmware doesn\'t say the module takes a new name and PIN. Older nRF modules and add-on modules are set up with their own tools.
Up to 25 characters; under 2 restores the default
Up to 6 digits, padded with zeros; empty turns the PIN off
The module restarts with the new settings. If this phone is connected over Bluetooth, connect again; with a PIN set, Android asks for it when pairing.
The module restarts. A Bluetooth link to this controller drops, and phones that paired with the old PIN have to pair again.
Start pairing, then turn the remote on (or hold its pairing button) within the window. The controller stores the remote and only listens to it from then on.
The controller stored the remote. Check its throttle in Inputs before riding.
The window ran out before a remote asked to pair. Turn the remote on sooner, or choose a longer window.
It has no nRF radio, or its firmware can\'t pair a VESC Remote.
It started listening but never said how pairing ended. This hardware probably can\'t pair a VESC Remote.
Bit rate and mode of the CAN bus between controllers
Every device on the bus has to use the same rate. The change is broadcast to every VESC on the bus, which all switch a second later and store it.

Every VESC on the bus switches. A device that misses the broadcast, or isn\'t a VESC (BMS, display, other CAN gear), stays at the old rate and drops off the bus until you change it by hand over USB. Needs firmware 6.06 or newer.
The bus switched to the new rate
This mode stops VESC commands on the bus
The app can\'t reach other controllers through this one, and they can\'t reach it. Change it back over a direct link to this controller.
The controller stores the new mode in its app configuration.

The controller stores the new mode. From then on VESC commands don\'t pass through its CAN bus: other controllers become unreachable from here, and if you are connected through another controller, this one does too.
Let desktop VESC Tool reach this controller through the phone, on WiFi or through a TCP hub

The phone relays everything between VESC Tool and the controller. It keeps working here at the same time, so avoid changing settings from both sides at once. Sharing stops when you disconnect or close the app.
VESC Tool sees the simulated controller, which is handy for trying the setup.
VESC Tool on a computer in the same WiFi finds the phone under Connection, TCP, or connects to the address and port shown once sharing runs.
The phone registers with a hub under an id and password; VESC Tool anywhere connects to the same hub with the same id and password.
At least 3 characters, the same in VESC Tool
Id, password and every packet cross the internet readable to anyone on the path. Use a password you use nowhere else, and stop sharing when done: whoever has the id and password can drive the motor.
